subject: Marketplace rate card, term options & approver matrix for Meditech
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@meditech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick clarifications on AWS Marketplace offer and approver path

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the call earlier. Procurement at Meditech asked for a concise write-up we can include with our vendor review. Two quick items they want clarified before we kick off the private offer:

1) Pricing cadence: do you support a 12-month and 24-month rate card? If so, what are the discount tiers for committed spend thresholds?
2) Buyer approvals: who needs to sign off on the AWS Marketplace PO on your side (seller-side approvals) and from our side — does the process differ if we choose a 24-month term vs 12-month?

If you can send a single-sheet summary and any compliance evidence we can attach to our procurement packet, that would speed things up.

Cheers,
Alice Chen
Senior Sourcing Manager
Meditech
(Attachment: procurement_template.docx)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@meditech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on AWS Marketplace offer and approver path

Hi Alice — great speaking earlier. High-level answers below; attaching a one-pager and the rate card for procurement.

Summary: we can do both 12- and 24-month seller-guided offers in AWS Marketplace. Pricing bands below are indicative — final private-offer price will be locked in the PO.

- 12-month: list price with a 10% volume discount for annual commit >= $150k; additional 5% discount for renewals signed inside the original 12-month window.
- 24-month: baseline 18% discount for commits >= $250k; step-downs to 22% at >= $500k.

Approval notes (seller side):
- Standard: Sales Ops escalates private offers > $100k to our Revenue Desk for review.
- Exceptions & custom term language escalate to Legal.

Buyer-side guidance (Meditech perspective):
- Procurement can approve standard AWS Marketplace PO up to $250k.
- CFO or delegated finance approver required for multi-year deals that exceed $250k total commitment (typical for 24-month with higher discounts).
- If you plan to route via your internal compliance (security evidence), include the AWS Marketplace evidence bundle we attached — it accelerates procurement reviews.

Attached: ratecard_v1.xlsx (rate bands + example TCV calculations), aws_evidence_bundle.zip (SOC2 summary + network diagram + dataflow).

Next steps: if you confirm target TCV and preferred term, Vanessa (cc'd) will run this against our pricing guardrails and Karthik will prep the seller-side approval packet. We can then issue the private offer and share the DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: ratecard_v1.xlsx)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 11:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Marketplace rate card, term options & approver matrix for Meditech

Vanessa / Karthik — forwarding Meditech's procurement ask (see thread). Quick asks:

1) Can Revenue Desk sign off on a 18% discount at $250k TCV for a 24-month seller-guided offer, or do we need manager-level approval?
2) Any recommended guardrails around billing cadence (AWS Marketplace supports monthly vs annual billing) — if they want monthly billing w/ a 24-month term we usually restrict larger discounts.
3) If Legal needs to clear term deviations (e.g., custom data retention or ingress/egress clauses) — flag now.

Context: Meditech is leaning toward a 24-month to get a lower per-token cost, but procurement wants confirmation on approver routing so they can align internal timelines. I attached our rate card and the compliance bundle.

Proposed approach: if Revenue Desk approves, we issue private offer at 18% with an explicit renewal clause (automatic renewal opt-in disabled) and require CFO sign-off on buyer side for TCV > $250k. If Revenue Desk passes, I'll create the private offer and route DocuSign.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turn so we don't lose momentum.

— Stephanie
(Attachment: aws_evidence_bundle.zip)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2027 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Marketplace rate card, term options & approver matrix for Meditech

Thanks for the context — happy to approve the 18% at $250k TCV for a 24-month private offer under these conditions:

- Finance must confirm internal recognition schedule (Meditech will need to confirm whether they want monthly USD billing or annual upfront). If monthly billing, reduce discount to 16%.
- Legal must pre-clear any non-standard data or retention language. Karthik, please attach a short Legal checklist in the approval packet (I see none in the current attachments beyond SOC2).
- Seller-side process: Revenue Desk approval is sufficient for pricing at this band; no C-level OK needed on our side, but escalate to Head of Sales if they request custom entitlements (SLA credits, indemnities).

Buyer-side guidance to give Meditech (I suggest we include in the one-pager):
- Procurement signature for PO on AWS Marketplace up to $250k TCV.
- CFO sign-off required for TCV > $250k or if the term extends beyond 24 months.
- If Procurement requests invoice-attachment evidence, point them to aws_evidence_bundle.zip and our compliance portal link.

Karthik — once you add the Legal checklist I will sign off in Revenue Desk and Stephanie can issue the offer.

-Vanessa
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(Thread metadata: internal participants only include Redwood employees. External attachments referenced are for procurement use.)
